profile.regional_context: Per Google's own data center location page, The Dalles facility, begun in 2006, was Google's first data center that the company built and operated itself, marking the start of Google building its own infrastructure rather than leasing it. Google reports more than $7 billion invested in Oregon since 2006, and began construction of a fourth building at the site in 2015. Google cited workforce, business-friendly policy, and energy infrastructure as its stated reasons for choosing the location. Local and national press (Fortune, OPB) have also covered water-use tension between Google and the City of The Dalles over the years.
profile.disclosure_policy: Google publishes aggregate state level investment figures on its data center location pages but does not publish exact addresses, square footage, or MW capacity for individual buildings
profile.facility_type_note: Part of Google's The Dalles, Wasco County, Oregon data center campus, historically Google's single most significant data center site.
